thread.title: Stocks Today: Exxon Mobil, JPMorgan Hit In Dow Jones; Facebook Rises | Investor's Business Daily

author: KEN SHREVE
title: Stocks Today: Exxon Mobil, JPMorgan Hit In Dow Jones; Facebook Rises | Investor's Business Daily
text:
It was a mostly quiet open for the stock market just after the opening bell Monday. But things were far from quiet in afternoon trading as major stock indexes moved off lows. Stocks today on the move in the Dow Jones included JPMorgan ( JPM ), UnitedHealth ( UNH ) and Exxon Mobil ( XOM ).
X After falling 1.3% intraday, the Nasdaq composite was down just 0.1%. The Dow Jones industrial average more than halved a 505-point intraday decline to 190 points. The blue-chip index was down 0.8%, while the S&P 500 eased 0.7%.
Homebuilders, oil and gas stocks, and specialty retailers lagged. At the New York Mercantile Exchange, U.S. crude oil futures were down 1.6% to $51.79 a barrel. Oil rebounded 3.3% last week after OPEC and allies agreed to cut output by 1.2 million barrels a day.
Apple ( AAPL ) moved back to nearly break-even after falling 3% intraday. Shares were weak early after the company suffered a legal setback in its dispute with Qualcomm ( QCOM ). A Citi price-target cut to 200 from 240 didn't help matters.

After crashing 6.6% last week, the Philadelphia Semiconductor index was up 1% in afternoon trading Monday.
Stocks Today: Nutrisystem Soars In the stock market today, shares of weight-management firm Nutrisystem ( NTRI ) surged 28% on news that Tivity Health ( TVTY ) is acquiring it for $1.4 billion in cash and stock. Tivity provides fitness and health-improvement programs in the U.S., but Tivity shareholders weren't happy about the deal. Shares of Tivity crashed more than 30% on the news.
Inside the MarketSmith Growth 250 , Tableau Software ( DATA ) was a nice gainer, up 2% to 125.90. After flashing a sell signal from the 118.18. buy point, Tableau reclaimed the buy point impressively and is holding near highs.
Some stocks today in the IBD 50 held up well, including Kirkland Gold ( KL ). The stock poked above the 23.96 entry in afternoon trading, but it's not a conviction breakout yet. Still, the stock looked poised for its eighth straight gain. Kirkland was featured in an IBD 50 Stocks To Watch column last week.
